sounds.intro: Welsh is spelled very regularly. The stress usually falls on the second-last syllable. The vowels "w" and "y" can be vowels. A word's first letter often changes (a "mutation") after some words, so you will see the same word in two spellings: cath, ei chath, fy nghath.
rows: "oo" as in "moon", or "w" before a vowel
"uh" in most words, "ee" in the last syllable
blow air past the sides of the tongue, an "hl" sound
like "eye" or "ay", depending on the region
notes: Welsh has two words for "you": "ti" for a friend or child and "chi" for strangers, elders and groups.
Most sentences use "mae" (is / are) in front of the subject: "Mae'r ci yn fawr" (the dog is big). "Dw i" is "I am", short for "rydw i".

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Welsh has no he / she difference for verbs, but the pronoun does: "e" or "fe" (he) and "hi" (she). The little form "ti" is for friends, "chi" for strangers, elders and groups.

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Many nouns add -au or -on: ci, cŵn (irregular), llyfr, llyfrau. After a number, the noun stays singular: dau lyfr (two book).

grammar.title: To be: bod
text: Welsh uses "bod" (to be). Present: dw i (I am), rwyt ti (you are), mae e / hi (he, she is), dyn ni (we are), dych chi (you are), maen nhw (they are). Before a noun, use "yn" or the word order of "ydy".

grammar.title: Having: gan, gyda
text: Welsh says "with me": mae gen i (I have), mae gen ti (you have), mae ganddo fe (he has), mae ganddi hi (she has), mae gynnon ni (we have), mae gynnoch chi (you have), mae ganddyn nhw (they have).

grammar.title: Present tense
text: Use "bod" + "yn" + the verb-noun. "Dw i'n bwyta" is I am eating (or I eat). The "yn" often joins the word before it: dw i'n, rwyt ti'n, mae e'n.

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: The verb comes first. Welsh order is verb, subject, object. The adjective follows the noun.

grammar.title: Negation
text: In the present, "dim" follows the subject: dw i ddim yn gweld (I am not seeing). The "dd" is a mutation of "dim". In the past, use "ches i ddim" (I did not get).
ex: dw i ddim yn siarad Saesneg
doo ee thim un SHAR-ad SIGHS-neg
dw i ddim yn ei hoffi
doo ee thim un ay HOF-ee
I do not have a car
mae e'n gweithio ar ddydd Sul
mine eh'n GOOITH-yo ar theeth seel
he does not work on Sundays
dyw e ddim yn gweithio ar ddydd Sul
dew eh thim un GOOITH-yo ar theeth seel

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: Swap the order: put "wyt" or "ydy" first and add the subject. "Wyt ti'n..." = are you...? A short answer repeats the verb: "Ydw" (I am), "Nac ydw" (I am not).
ex: ai dy lyfr di yw hwn?
ie duh hluvr dee yoo hoon

grammar.title: Possessives and liking
text: The possessive comes before the noun and changes its first letter: fy llyfr i (my book, with a nasal sound in speech), dy lyfr di (your book), ei lyfr e (his book), ei llyfr hi (her book).
ex: dw i wrth fy modd â phêl-droed
doo ee oorth vuh moth ah fayl-droyd

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: "Ti" is for friends and children. "Chi" is for strangers, older people and groups. The verb ending changes: wyt ti / ydych chi.

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: Past: add endings to the stem: es i (I went), est ti (you went), aeth e (he went). Future: bydda i + yn + the verb-noun: bydda i'n mynd (I will go).

grammar.title: Commands
text: Use the stem for "ti": dere (come), arhosa (wait). Add -wch for "chi": dewch (come), arhoswch (wait). To forbid, use "paid" (ti) or "peidiwch" (chi) + "â" + the verb-noun.

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: "Gallu" (can): alla i (I can), alli di (you can). "Mae'n rhaid i" (must): mae'n rhaid i fi fynd. "Eisiau" (want): dw i eisiau mynd.
ex: does dim hawl gyda ni i fynd
doys dim howl GUH-da nee ee veend
I do not want to eat
mae'n rhaid i fi weithio heddiw
mine rhide ee vee WEETH-yo HETH-yoo
does dim hawl gyda ti i redeg
doys dim howl GUH-da tee ee RED-eg

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: Welsh uses short words before the place: "yn" (in), "ar" (on), "wrth" (at, by), "o dan" (under), "wrth ymyl" (next to), "ger" (near), "i" (to), "o" (from). Many make the next word change its first letter.
ex: the book is on the table
the cat is under the table
mae'r gath o dan y bwrdd
mire gath oh dan uh boorth
the shop is next to the bank
mae'r siop wrth ymyl y banc
mire shop oorth UM-il uh bank
the park is near the station
dyn ni'n cwrdd yn y bore
din neen koordh un uh BOR-eh
mae'r wers am naw o'r gloch
mire wers am now or glokh
the key is in the bag

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: Add -ach for "more" and -af for "the most": mawr, mwy (irregular), mwyaf. Regular: cyflym, cyflymach, cyflymaf. "Than" is "na". "As ... as" is "mor ... â".
ex: mae hwn yn well na hwnna
mine hoon un wehlh nah HOON-a
mae hwn yn waeth na hwnna
mine hoon un wighth nah HOON-a
mae Tashkent yn fwy na Samarkand
mine tash-KENT un vooee nah sa-mar-KAND
